header.name: Cell Biology and Biochemistry
header.description: This is a foundational core course for post-graduate CB students with an engineering and science background that aims to provide a good qualitative and quantitative understanding of cell biology and biochemistry. The major focus is to a) cover the most important concepts in cell biology like cell structure, its division and movement b) relate structure of biomolecules to function in biochemistry by taking examples of DNA, proteins carbohydrates and lipids, and their polymers c) provide quantitative understanding tof metabolism and signal transduction mechanisms using the tools of thermodynamics,and enzyme kinetics.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students will identify four imortant classes of biomolecules, its strucure, function and their polymerization/aggregation properties. They will understand the importance of stereochemical properties.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students can write simple emprical equations to explain the types of weak forces that plays an important role in stability of biomolecules. They will perform simple simulation in Python to visualize the molecules and calculate the forces and potentials.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students will apply concepts of thermodynamics to biomolecules to understand the directionality of reactions and understand the role of coupled reactions. They will understand equilibrium, reversibility and irreversibility of metabolic reactions.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students will derive enzyme kinetic equations under different scenarios and apply it to signaling and metabolic networks. Glycolysis will be taken as one specific example. They will also understand the time-scales of the reactions.

outcomes.label: CO5
outcomes.raw_text: Students will understand the role of cell as molecular nanomachine that carries out important tasks like division, fusion, and movement. They will understand the role of neuronal cells as information carrier and transfer.

lecture_topics: Overview of cell biology and Biochemistry
Structure of lipids, carbohydrates, amino acids and nucleic acids
Specification of stereoisomers and its implication in drug efficacy
Revision of bond angles, bond length in biomolecules and its implications in stability
Introduction to Intra and inter molecular forces, Weak forces like vander-waals, electrostatic forces etc
Writing empirical equations that describe these forces and potentials
Introduction to dihedral angles and Ramachandran plots
Introduction to biothermodynamics
Introduction to enzyme kinetics
Derivation of Lineweaver-Burke plots
Inhibition dynamics
Introduction to Hill's equation
Switch, graded response and ultrasensitivity
Introduction to metabolism
Application of kinetics and thermodynamics to carbohydrate metabolism
Introduction to cell as a nanomachine
Prokaryotic and eukaryotic Cell division cycle
Their similarities and differences
Importance of compartmentalization
Microtuble dynamics and its implications in cancer dynamics
Neurons as transfer of information and derivation of Nernst-planck equations

resources.title: (i) Biochemistry by Garrett and Grisham (ii) Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry, Nelson and Cox
Trends in Cell biology, Trends in Biochemical sciences
Physical biology of the cell, Jane Kondev, Julie Theriot, and Rob Phillips.
